item1_purge_basis.answer: Neither constant rate is right. The vented mass is the purge-record mass M(t), not a rate times t. The records (vented_mass_brackets_v2p4a, SIM on ASSUMED Cd 0.70 and slip brackets) start with vapour at the taps (8.49 g/s line) and turn to liquid (31.24 g/s line); M(2.5 s) <= 72.93 g (open element; barrier 72.06 g). After 2.5 s the marginal rate is at most the all-liquid rate 31.24 g/s (two taps at 0.707 mm, Cd 0.70 ASSUMED, Dyer 56843 kg/m2s at the coast state 46.45 bar, 289.5 K: an upper-bound flux); the maximum record itself ends at 30.6 g/s (2.4-2.5 s). 29.2 g/s x t is right only at t = 2.5 s and understates the slope after it by <= 2.0 g/s; 31.44-32.0 g/s x t applies the all-liquid rate from t = 0, i.e. assumes the line holds no vapour when the purge starts, which is the condition the purge exists to remove: it overstates M(2.5 s) by 5.7 g (+7.8 %). The SIL liquid rate (31.44 g/s nominal, 31.86 g/s maximum in S12 v2.9) is 0.6-2.0 % above the Combustion all-liquid rate: a plant-state/flux-model difference (SIL flux 57187 kg/m2s at Cd 0.70 on the 1.0 mm area), not a basis disagreement.

The ECU commands it at E1, holds it to E2 and, in the LEAD 186 (2) command hold with Pc invalid, keeps it (no open-loop map lookup in the hold). CF-3 measures mdot and the load-cell F at the commanded lift with the encoder lift recorded (start-lift acceptance, cold_flow_start_lift_v2p4b).

item3_E2_rule.statement: The ECU E2 comes earlier than the model E2 by at most 14.7 ms (model 16.5-27.0 ms after the light at 0.2192 mm; relative rule >= 12.3 ms by construction, 14-16 ms in the grain_q1d runs). The gap arrival after the light does not depend on the E2 rule for the held profile and moves earlier by at most the same shift for the ramp profiles (the ramp starts at E2). So the hold counted from the ECU E2 is at most the table hold plus the shift: bound values below (rounded up to 10 ms). P(success) and the trip class of each record do not change; for a given H the split between released-then-A3 and A3-before-release moves by <= the shift. The release-term reading of the table (Pc >= 3.0 bar abs, R3-12 note) is unchanged.

kStartRamp_Nps = 2500 N/s.source_text: Start ramp: after E2, and after the release of the LEAD 186 (2) command hold, the thrust command rises at <= 2500 N/s (5 F_max per second) from the thrust at the start lift (REPORT v2.4a §7.4 step 6; Combustion v2.1 start sequence). Basis: (a) it equals the actuator rate under load required of ENG-03 (>= 5 F_max/s = 2500 N/s, LEAD 2026-10-13, bench plan v2), so the command never outruns the actuator during the start; (b) a full 62.5 -> 500 N ramp at 2500 N/s has t10-90 = 0.140 s, inside the ENG-03 t10-90 <= 0.15 s (gnc.json v2), the slowest ramp meeting it being 2333 N/s; (c) every start-timing result uses it (start_latency_v2p4 with a 1000 N/s slow case, REPORT Tables 2.16-2.17, release_hold_v2p4b ramp profiles).
kStartRamp_Nps = 2500 N/s.tag: DESIGN (Combustion v2.1 choice) with DERIVED consistency checks; not a physical limit

kSparkTrain_s = 0.5 s.source_text: Spark train: 50 Hz, 50 mJ, from E0 + 0.02 s for at most 0.5 s (to E0 + 0.52 s), stopped earlier at E2 (REPORT §7.4 steps 2 and 6; igniter sequence v2.2). Basis: it covers the torch-light window with margin (torch gate E1 by E0 + 0.16 s; E0 -> E1 median 0.09 s) and re-sparks a torch that blows out before the main light while the torch runs (SOL1 off at E2, torch off by E0 + 0.6 s). The latest E2 (0.626 s from E0 on the purged relight) can fall after the train: the torch then runs without spark until E2 or 0.6 s; torch stability under the main flow is an IGN-1 item (FA-1 FM3).

firmware: [COMB] ... or before Pc exceeds this (propane vapour pressure)
kPropaneOffPcAbs_Pa = 5 bar abs.source_text: Propane solenoid (SOL2) closed at E0 + 0.40 s or before the chamber pressure exceeds 5 bar abs, whichever first; in the v2.4 sequence SOL2 closes within 20 ms of SOL1 at E2 (Pc about 3 bar) and this is the backstop. Basis: the propane supply is self-pressurised at its vapour pressure (4.74 bar abs at 0 C, 6.37 at 10 C, 8.36 at 20 C, CoolProp); with Pc above the supply pressure, chamber gas can flow back into the propane line. 5 bar abs is the propane vapour pressure at 1.7 C, so the rule protects a supply at or above about 2 C (REPORT §7.2: torch Pc 3 bar stays below the propane vapour pressure down to about 0 C).
kPropaneOffPcAbs_Pa = 5 bar abs.tag: DERIVED (CoolProp propane saturation) on the DESIGN torch; the minimum propane temperature (about 2 C) is an implied operating limit, TO-VERIFY against the founders' propane conditioning

kPintleToIgnitionLift_s = 0.12 s.source_text: Ignition-lift slot of a timing-only (ground) start: the pintle is commanded to the ignition lift at E0 + 0.12 s when no E1 sensor result is used. It is the v2.2 sequence value: torch confirmed by E0 + 0.10 s plus 20 ms. In flight (v2.8 on) the lift command is issued at E1 (torch confirmed on P_torch AND photodiode), not at 0.12 s. The unlit-inventory figures are counted from the lift command (REPORT §2.8, W from the lift command) and do not depend on the slot.

history: Before the first start the passage holds pad air at ambient pressure (DESIGN: the port is open to the chamber).

First burn (A1 0-3.5 s): chamber pressure compresses the passage contents toward the transducer and head-face gas enters; at 25 bar abs the pad air keeps 4-10 % of the volume (isothermal-adiabatic). The passage walls stay at 20-22 C through MECO (A1 SIM monitors); the radial thermal time of the 1 mm-radius passage at 25 bar is about 0.2 s, so the gas sits at the wall temperature. Diffusion over the burn (about 1.5 mm at 25 bar) and pressure pumping mix the pad-air slug with head-face gas.

MECO: the chamber vents to ambient; the passage gas re-expands and leaves mouth-first. With plug flow the pad air would refill the passage; with the mixing above the passage holds pad air mixed with first-burn head-face gas (N2, CO2, CO, H2, O2, water to saturation, N2O). The proportions are MISSING (not modelled).

Coast (MECO to RELIGHT 18.7 s, A1): the walls warm to 32.2-51.9 C (A1 SIM; +4-11 % gas expansion, outflow); the descent from apogee raises ambient pressure by about 3 % (inflow of about 3 % of the volume: chamber gas = air drawn through the nozzle, post-shutdown N2O from the seat annulus, grain pyrolysis gas); diffusion at 1 bar homogenises over about 17 mm of the 56 mm.
PURGE (E0 - 2.9 s to E0 - 0.05 s): the bleed taps vent the feed upstream of the seated pintle overboard (REPORT §2.7, H15); no flow passes the chamber, so the passage is unchanged.

Relight before the light: cold N2O (vapour first on an unpurged line) enters the chamber; the cold-flow chamber pressure (about 1.5 bar abs) pushes head-face gas (flashed N2O vapour at T_sat 191 K, torch products) into about 25-33 % of the volume.

FA-1 rise (light to peak, construct t_f 1-4 ms): at the median (48.2 bar abs) and maximum (88.0 bar abs) construct peaks the relight-instant gas is compressed into the closed-end 1.1-6.3 % of the passage (isothermal-adiabatic) and the cold-flow gas into the next 0.6-1.8 %; 92-98 % of the passage at the peak is head-face gas that entered during the rise (lower peaks leave a larger closed-end share). The core is compressed adiabatically: thermal penetration in 4 ms is <= 0.09 mm at the peak pressure and <= 0.13 mm early in the rise, against the 1.0 mm radius. What enters during the rise is the gas at the port mouth (r 20.5 mm on the head face): the lumped construct does not predict it (its head node burns every source at the case O/F by convention): MISSING.

answer.at_FA1_instant: c in the passage core at the FA-1 peak (construct head peaks 22.2-88.0 bar abs, median 48.2) depends on what enters during the rise (MISSING): burned products 1049-1136 m/s (frozen, T_HP, O/F 3-8; higher after compression); unburned N2O that flashed at <= 46.5 bar and was compressed isentropically >= 202 m/s (entry 46.5 bar, peak 48.0 bar); N2O at the wall temperature (wall layer, or a slow rise) 203-383 m/s at the median and maximum peaks; the single-phase N2O minimum anywhere in the peak range is 181 m/s (72bar, 309.2 K, gas), 185 m/s below 70 bar; the compressed relight-instant air at the closed end 350-677 m/s (isothermal-isentropic).
answer.bound: Combustion cannot bound c better than 222-400 m/s in the direction that matters. For a gas-filled passage the lower end is about 181 m/s (N2O near its critical point, a peak near 72.5 bar with the gas near 310 K) and about 202 m/s for N2O vapour compressed from saturation (the core of a 1-4 ms rise), not 222 m/s; if liquid N2O reaches the passage (spray or condensate below the critical pressure) the two-phase sound speed is far lower and is not bounded here. The upper end is about 1136 m/s (burned products), not 400 m/s; a higher c only shortens the period. Design value for a <= 1 ms check: c_min = 181 m/s with the passage kept free of liquid N2O (CONDITIONAL; TO-VERIFY at IGN-1 / B-PC-1 with the port ringing recorded).
answer.period_scaling: on Mechanical's CC-1 V_end = 0 row (lossless 1-D, uniform gas: T = 0.992 ms at 222 m/s, T proportional to 1/c): T = 1.217 ms at 181 m/s (c_min), 1.090 ms at 202 m/s (isentropic N2O), 0.210 ms at 1049 m/s (products). c >= 220.2 m/s is needed for T <= 1 ms on CC-1 at V_end = 0, so CC-1 does not meet 1 ms at c_min; Mechanical recomputes the CC-2 passage (<= 30 mm) at c_min.
